instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high until it's glistening.

Add 4 hot dogs, spaced apart. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shifting them about every minute, until they're plump and browned on all sides. They only need to reach 140°F in the middle and they're already cooked, so you're heating and browning them.
Transfer them to a plate and wipe out the pan. Add the remaining tablespoon of oil and cook the other 4 the same way.
Warm the buns in the empty pan, cut side down, for about 30 seconds.
Serve in the buns with mustard and ketchup.
method_notes: Only The Modern Proper's page could be read with ratings (5 from 1 rating, so the fallback applies). It gives three ways to cook hot dogs; the skillet method is used here, searing them in a little olive oil for 3 to 4 minutes until plumped and browned. Taste of Home also boils (4 to 6 minutes) or splits and browns them in butter, but those had no ratings. Check the hot dog and bun labels for dairy and nuts.
